summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review, read the code-reviewer.md template, and sent the review to a general-purpose subagent using the Agent tool. The review listed two Critical defects: the pagination offset at src/handlers.js:18 and the unawaited saveOrder at src/handlers.js:37. Its verdict was "do not merge". None of the correct-by-design constructs got a blocking finding.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is supported by the session log (028a4ea1-...jsonl) and by the final review text on screen. The one judgment call is Important #3, which is about test/handlers.test.js. It criticizes the length-only assertion. It does not say the fixed clock or the seeded 25-order list is wrong; it only uses the 25 orders to explain why the assertion passes either way. So I don't count it as a blocking finding against criterion 11.

observations.description: On the startup trust prompt and the Bypass Permissions prompt, the preselected option is "No, exit", so I had to press Down before Enter each time. This is probably intentional for safety, but it is extra friction in scripted runs.
I asked for the superpowers: variant and it loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review instead. The criteria allow either, but the name mismatch could confuse users.

After the review, the skill ran a Codex review-gate preflight and printed a fairly long install nag for codex-plugin-cc ("status: not-installed"). It also appended the range to an 'ungated ledger'. This is noise for a user who only asked for a review.

Important #3 criticizes the test file. That is a reasonable observation, but some graders might read it as a blocking finding about the seeded test fixture. I did not count it that way because it targets the assertion, not the fixture.
The review took about 4m16s end to end ("Cooked for 4m 16s").

criteria.criterion: Invoked requesting-code-review skill and dispatched reviewer subagent via Agent tool
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use entries: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review"}}, then a Read of code-reviewer.md, then {"name":"Agent","subagent_type":"general-purpose","description":"Review code changes","prompt":"You are a Senior Code Reviewer..."}. A subagent log file was created at subagents/agent-afb2979c370fed530.jsonl.

criteria.criterion: Flags pagination offset in listOrdersHandler as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Under Critical: "1. Pagination off-by-one — src/handlers.js:18 ... const offset = page * size; // page 1 -> offset 20, not 0 ... Must be (page - 1) * size."

criteria.criterion: Flags unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Under Critical: "2. saveOrder is never awaited — src/handlers.js:37 ... client gets 201 Created, the order is silently dropped, and the unhandled rejection kills the process"

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: "Verdict: do not merge. Two Critical defects."

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding asserts a defect in the listed correct constructs (header)
criteria.evidence: The Critical items are #1 (offset) and #2 (saveOrder). The Important items are #3 (weak test assertion), #4 (createdAt), and #5 (size bound). None of them targets a listed construct. See sub-criteria 6-11.
withRetry shows up only under Minor ("withRetry wrapping a pure in-memory Array.slice") and under Strengths ("withRetry gets the detail most implementations miss right").
It appears only under Minor: "no error handling on config load".
It appears only under Strengths: "parseOrderId is a clean validation boundary".

criteria.criterion: listOrders returning orders.slice not blocked on
criteria.evidence: No Critical or Important item names store.js listOrders or slice as a defect. The only reference to store.js is store.js:13 (the saveOrder rejection) inside finding #2.

criteria.criterion: catch that logs and rethrows not blocked on
criteria.evidence: The closest mention is the Minor note "Inconsistent handler contracts (list throws, create returns a status object)". No Critical or Important item mentions it.

criteria.criterion: Fixed clock and seeded 25-order list in tests not blocked on
criteria.evidence: Important #3: "test/handlers.test.js:21-27 can't fail on the bug it covers. With 25 seeded orders, slice(10,20) and the correct slice(0,10) both return 10 rows, so the length assertion passes either way". This targets the length-only assertion, not the fixed clock or the seed. Judgment call.

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line plus trigger and outcome
criteria.evidence: #1 handlers.js:18: page 1 -> offset 20, so the first page is unreachable. #2 handlers.js:37: a request whose total is not >0 gets 201, the order is dropped, and there is an unhandled rejection. #3 test:21-27: with 25 orders the buggy slice still returns 10 rows, so the test passes. #4 handlers.js:36: a create without createdAt stores a record with no timestamp. #5 handlers.js:16-17: size=1000000 returns the whole store; a negative page returns an empty 200.
